summary: The stages of compilation — lexical analysis, syntax analysis, code generation and optimisation — with worked examples of each.

blocks.content:
flowchart LR
  S[Source code] --> L[Lexical analysis] --> Y[Syntax analysis] --> G[Code generation] --> O[Optimisation] --> M[Object / machine code]
  L -. symbol table .- Y
blocks.caption: From source code to machine code

blocks.title: What each stage does
rows: Removes spaces and comments; splits code into tokens (keywords, identifiers, operators, literals); builds the **symbol table**
Checks tokens follow the **grammar rules** of the language
Produces machine code / intermediate code for each construct
Makes code faster or smaller without changing what it does

blocks.content: if (count > 10) total = total + count;   // check limit
blocks.caption: Source line

blocks.content: The parser checks that the tokens form a valid statement according to the grammar, and builds a tree.

flowchart TB
  A["="] --> T1[total]
  A --> P["+"]
  P --> T2[total]
  P --> C[count]
blocks.caption: Parse tree for total = total + count

blocks.content: `if (count > 10 total = total + count;` passes lexical analysis (all tokens are valid) but **fails syntax analysis** — a bracket is missing.
Each node of the parse tree is turned into machine-code (or assembly) instructions.

LDA total     ; load total into the accumulator
ADD count     ; add count
STO total     ; store the result in total
blocks.caption: Code generated for total = total + count

items: Memory addresses are allocated for variables (from the symbol table).
The output is **object code**, which the **linker** joins with library code to create an executable file.

items.title: Constant folding
items.content: Calculate constant expressions at compile time: `x = 60 * 60 * 24` → `x = 86400`.

items.title: Dead code elimination
items.content: Remove code that can **never run** or whose result is never used: `a = 5; if (a != 5) { … }` — the block is removed.

items.title: Loop optimisation
items.content: Move calculations that do not change out of a loop (**loop-invariant code motion**).

items.title: Redundant instruction removal
items.content: `STO x` followed immediately by `LDA x` — the `LDA` is unnecessary.

blocks.caption: Before and after optimisation

blocks.title: Benefits and drawbacks of optimisation
rows: Debugging is harder — compiled code differs from the source
Aggressive optimisation can introduce subtle bugs
